analysis.title: Nomura - McElligott - USE YOUR WORDS - 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: Initial equity and bond rally and USD selloff after the midterms is read as standard tail-hedge unwinding. Puts were monetized after the initial 'Blue Tsunami' selloff, and constructive call-spread trades are the preferred client play into year-end on post-midterm seasonality.

Gold up about 3% is read as signaling no tolerance for high deficit and fiscal spending under a future Democratic regime. It may also reflect easing of speculated selling from GCC countries and Iran if Trump's Iran resolve is weaker.

Trump said he has no immediate plans to launch strikes on Iran after the midterms. This supports the repricing lower of oil over the past week, lower yields and a lower USD, which together ease US financial conditions.

One rationale for the rally is a belief that the election results will force a moderation of US datacenter buildout. That would calm hyperscaler capex 'prisoner's dilemma' concerns, ease credit and equity issuance and FCF burn fears, reduce pressure on duration and crowding-out risk to USTs, and ease 'higher neutral rate' concerns.

MSFT, AMZN, META and GOOGL aligned with Sierra Club, League of Conservation Voters and NRDC on a 'Responsible Data Center Development Collaborative' framework (per TheHill.com). Under Democratic power this can speed a slower buildout and reduce the risk of a full stop to data center development.

Concerns about a swing to socialism, higher taxes and wealth redistribution moderated after the apparent blocking of the California wealth tax and nationwide pushback on property tax increases. McElligott reads the election as an anti-Trump referendum, not a capitulation to Democratic Socialism.
The net effect is a modest tailwind for incrementally lower rates, but not a regime change or new bull-market catalyst for USTs. The rates outlook remains two-way and opaque.

Offsetting forces on rates: growth may cool if datacenter capex slows, but the AI datacenter hard-stop risk is reduced. Debt issuance remains robust (META with a EUR deal), higher financing costs and wider credit spreads are a drag, and inflation remains too high. Rates likely keep chopping with a slight bias to lower yields.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Read as no tolerance for perpetual high deficit spending under a future Democratic regime, and possibly easing GCC and Iran selling pressure.
Lower oil, yields and USD are easing conditions after recent tightening tied to AI-thesis cracks and an inflation and hawkish impulse.

risk_factors: Rates outlook remains two-way and opaque.

Robust debt issuance, higher financing costs and wider credit spreads act as a slow drag.

vol_and_positioning: Tail hedges came off after the initial 'Blue Tsunami' selloff, with puts monetized. This is typical of hedge behavior over the past decade (short windows to monetize equity downside and VIX upside).
Constructive call-spread trades are the preferred client play into year-end, supported by post-midterm seasonality and the narrative moderation after the recent degrossing purge.
geopolitical: Trump said he has no immediate plans to launch strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.
Possible easing of speculated selling pressure from GCC countries and Iran if Trump's Iran resolve is weaker.
Midterm results described as a 'Blue Tsunami' and an anti-Trump referendum.

tension_points.bull_case: A forced moderation of datacenter buildout calms hyperscaler capex race concerns, eases credit and equity issuance and FCF burn fears, and takes pressure off duration. The hyperscaler collaboration with environmental groups avoids a full stop.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth expectations may cool as the data center and hyperscaler capex train slows under Democratic control, and a hard stop could trigger a growth scare.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A full stop to data center development, described as a left-tail risk that would elicit an economic growth scare.
